reviews.title: Buggy and causes iOS problems
reviews.text:
I rarely write reviews, this is my very first review on a 10 year old account. Your app is so buggy and beyond a joke for the cost that I felt compelled to write this. 

The fundamental feature is flawed. Opal has no idea in real time how long you’ve been using an app. Yesterday it thought I had been using Instagram for over 30 mins and it locked me out, despite iOS screen time and the Opal app itself only showing 26 mins. Today I used Instagram for 50 mins with the same 30 min rule. The block came in 20 mins late. I wished to continue using Instagram, so I had to wait to unlock it. I went back to Instagram and was immediately locked out again. This happened 4 times in a row. Opal forces you to wait to unlock. That’s great, but not when I’ve had to do it 4 times in a row because your own app doesn’t know how to run its fundamental service. 

The cherry on top is my spotlight search started bugging out for the first time in the two years I’ve had my phone. I swipe down to search for an app, the keyboard won’t show, the search bar is all black. My phone will then freeze and I have to lock it. Uninstalling the Opal app fixed this. 

In the 5 mins I’ve been writing this review, I received two notifications from Opal saying “I’ve hit my daily limit” on Instagram (the rule). I AM LITERALLY IN THE APP STORE writing a review, not on Instagram. 

I am genuinely baffled this company goes so hard on advertising a polished product when it’s beyond bugged and broken. 

I feel scammed that

reviews.title: A bit scammy
reviews.text:
It’s a very basic screen time monitoring app, that doesn’t do much else than the native screen time feature for iOS already does. 

The way it measures success is pretty unsophisticated considering the subscription price. For example, the way it measures phone pickups makes no sense at all. Some days I have a “slow down” message for 10 pickups, while in others, it seems ok when I’m at 30 pick ups at the same time of day. There is no explicit logic to what determines the label: is it my overall score/average, is it across my cohort? Or is it just arbitrary? 

There’s also no evolution in measurement. If my screen time this week is X, then it will be compared to what I declared what my screen time was at setup. Weeks later, my progress will still be measured against that figure, instead of tracking week on week. Again, the native feature on iPhone does it better. 

The only reason I’m giving this a second star is because the UI looks great, and the ability to create different rule blocks with different strictness levels is helpful. 

Will not be renewing my subscription as I’m sure there will not be any significant changes in the next year or so that justify the price.

reviews.text:
I actually do appreciate Opal, in general. It’s definitely helped me cut down on screentime. Was disappointed tho, that they’re taking the typical bogus approach to customer service by making themselves as unreachable to customers as possible. All I wanted was to send a quick message to the design team, and got stuck in some loop of community forums. I am not wasting my time on that BS. Seems rather ironic that a company claiming to help keep people off their screens would add layers of app garbage for what could just be a simple contact form— click and send. Disappointing. 

And all I had to say, as feedback, was that the backdrop has switched to an ocean scene, but it’s clearly something like AI. The sound doesn’t align with the scene, and it’s clearly a split screen-the same waves mirrored on both sides. Believe me, your customers do spend enough time in nature to know the difference between real ocean and fake. And I will not support AI in any way shape or form, so if this continues, you’ll have lost me. 

There’s also no way to mute the fake ocean sounds. If I’m checking my apps in public, I don’t need extra noise. Design a way to permanently mute the sounds in settings. And don’t waste our time with useless customer service blocks. It just tells me you’re eating up over $100 a year without wanting to actually serve your customers.

I don’t ever write reviews, but I just want to say when I found opal it was the best app I’ve ever downloaded. It was perfect for screen time monitoring and blocking. It used to be very easy to use and navigate. You used to be able to organize your apps by least to most distracting and also remove certain apps like Navigation/GPS or Music from your screen time. 

Now, everything is counted in your screen time, and even if I’m not using an app but it’s running in the background, like Life360, it counts that as screen time, which, sorry, is kind of absurd. I’m obviously not scrolling on life360 for fourteen hours. 

Also, since the big Opal update a few weeks or months back, certain features just haven’t been working as they used to, and the interface is much more confusing. reviews.title: Awful confusing app.

This app makes no sense at all. It presets times for you - why can’t I say what times I want to block certain apps during the set up? I had to send an important message to someone and it took me a few minutes to work out how to unblock the app.

It also congratulated me on using it for 2 days - when it was my first day. Something clearly isn’t right with it.

£99 for a year is a crazy amount of money when you can block apps yourself using iOS. Just go to Settings then select “Screen Time”. You can block apps at certain times there and also create limits for other apps. I’m doing that - saving £99 a year and it’s a lot clearer to understand.

reviews.title: You had one job (it wasn’t more shiny rocks)
reviews.text:
Bugs ruined it, just nothing I could do for a couple hours as I was locked out of my ‘distracting apps’ while the Opal app tells me they’re all available and to reload the app (doesn’t work). 

Opal sends lots of notifications and is just an effort to use because of the lack of flexibility in blocking options. Missing some really obvious features and what did it for me after a couple hundred days religiously using the app was just the recurring waiting screens of slimy rock telling me to breathe. I’d just have to keep pressing unblock in all the different ways until eventually something gave. 

Also I never cared about streaks or getting more rocks. Certainly not as much as I just wanted the app to function as it should. The job this app is intended to do is such an important one these days, so the fact that it landed short though AI design and sloppy features made the failure feel ironic and more disappointing than if any old app missed the mark.

reviews.text:
Update: 
It’s been two whole weeks and Opal has still been unable to resolve the issue where my subscription doesn’t work. 
I’ve been given the same set of instructions multiple times, all to no avail. 
It’s quite disappointing that I’ve had to constantly chase down support for answers and help. 
Also, if the new app wasn’t stable yet, why not ensure it is before pushing it out and causing major inconvenience for users? 

 I’m not going to rate this yet because I’ve been using Opal for long and it’s served me well, but this new update has a confusing interface. 

The main goal of the app is to set blockers and timers, so why is the user being inundated with various categories of information that doesn’t serve any purpose for them? 
Secondly, the quick time that aren’t tied to any set “rules” are gone. If a timer is running, I no longer have access to Opal. If this is still possible to do, it’s entirely difficult to navigate how this works with the new design. 

Thirdly, you should have provided a guided tour or a wizard setup since this change is quite drastic. You didn’t inform your users beforehand about the update; you make significant changes to the experience, and then expect them to figure it out themselves. 

This is not the way to go about it. Please do better.

reviews.text:
I genuinely don’t understand how this app has such a high rating.

I spent HOURS setting everything up because the concept is amazing. Beautiful UI, great ideas… and then everything completely fell apart.

Within less than ONE DAY:
❌ WhatsApp got blocked even though I had used it for less than 20 minutes.
❌ Instagram was permanently blocked even though I hadn’t opened it ONCE that day.
❌ I suddenly couldn’t create any more rules because Opal claimed iOS had reached its limit.
❌ I deleted rules.
❌ I paused rules.
❌ I upgraded to the Pro trial.
❌ I restarted my phone.
❌ I used the built-in “Reload Opal” button.

Nothing fixed it.

The app basically soft-locked itself.

A productivity app has ONE job:

Its rules need to be reliable.

If time limits trigger randomly, apps get blocked for no reason, and new rules stop working entirely, then the whole purpose of the app is gone.

I wanted to love Opal.

Instead, I wasted hours configuring rules only to delete the app the same day.

Beautiful design. Fantastic marketing. Completely unreliable core functionality. I’m sad for people actually spending Hundreds of dollars into this piece of garbage WOWOWOW

0/5. Not recommended. Don’t waste your time!!!

reviews.title: Deleted after new update— no more app exclusions
reviews.text: As someone who only started using Opal very recently, I was super happy with it. It helped reduce my screen time by 3 hours daily average in a week, and I loved how easy the user interface was. I was especially happy with the option to exclude certain apps from your screen time. As a crocheter, I often have patterns pulled up on my phone, and sometimes it will be on for 2+ hours a day if I’m really in the groove. I loved that Opal allowed me to remove the Preview app from my screen time, since I wasn’t really using my phone for more than a few minutes in those passive hours. After their new 4.0 update, they’ve not only removed this feature, but generally have just made the whole app far more confusing and unusable (or time consuming to use, which is a little ironic). I’m a firm believer in “if it ain’t broke don’t fix it”, and I feel like this update was truly the epitome of that saying. I’m very annoyed that I just paid for a year long subscription of an app that I’ve now deleted, but it’s really not worth keeping at this point. I’ll be trying BePresent or other screentime focus apps, because Opal really isn’t it.

reviews.title: Great App, Terrible Redesign
reviews.text:
I originally loved Opal because it helped me stay focused and reduce the impact of today’s increasingly addictive digital culture. Its App UI was not well designed but it worked. As an entrepreneur, it became an important part of my daily routine.
Unfortunately, the recent redesign has been incredibly disappointing. Users were given no meaningful warning, no transition period, and no option to continue using the previous interface while adapting to the new one. Instead, loyal customers were forced into an entirely unfamiliar experience overnight.
The new UI feels visually overwhelming and unnecessarily complicated. I don’t need stories, gems, or additional layers of gamification—I simply need clear, reliable controls to block distracting apps and reclaim my attention.
What’s most frustrating is that this change appears to ignore basic human-centered design principles. Major product changes should be introduced thoughtfully, with communication, onboarding, and user choice. Instead, users are expected to relearn everything immediately, with no direct feedback channel beyond a forum.
After years of enjoying and recommending Opal, I will not be renewing my subscription. I sincerely hope Apple or another company provides a simpler, more user-focused alternative for managing screen time and digital well-being.

Setzt man sich ein „Tageslimit“ von X Minuten um eine App zu benutzen, dann ist die App teilweise direkt gesperrt, auch wenn man an dem Tag 0 Minuten Bildschirmzeit auf dieser App hat. Das wäre nicht so schlimm wenn es ab und zu passiert, es ist aber eher die Norm und nicht die Ausnahme. Macht man innerhalb eines Blocks eine Pause, passiert es auch häufiger, dass wenn diese vorbei ist, der Block nicht mehr richtig funktioniert, (die Pause geht unendlich lang weiter) wodurch die App quasi nonexistent wird. Die Leute die für so eine Performance 100€ im Jahr bezahlen (manchmal auf 50€ reduziert) tun mir wirklich leid. Gnadenlose Abzocke für so eine App dermaßen viel Geld zu verlangen, ein Bloom oder Brick ist definitiv eher zu empfehlen.
